newsitem.title: FRANCE: French old-crop wheat firmer, maize slips.
newsitem.headline: French old-crop wheat firmer, maize slips.

text.p: Old-crop wheat prices rose further on Thursday in thin trade, helped by short-covering and a lack of sellers while new-crop wheat prices remained steady, dealers said.
But old and new maize prices in southwestern ports slipped as farmers turned sellers to make room in silos ahead of the new wheat harvest, they said.
Rouen wheat for May delivery was bid at 855 francs per tonne, up five francs on Wednesday, while June wheat was unchanged at 855 francs, having risen 20 francs since the start of the week.
These prices should deter farmers from selling any wheat into French intervention stores during the season ending May 31, dealers said.
Rouen wheat for September-December delivery fetched 880-885 francs per tonne, depending on silos, unchanged on Wednesday.
Old-crop fob Atlantic maize was "massively" offered at 870 francs per tonne and bid at 860 francs. Buyers were bidding 870 francs the previous day.
Fob Atlantic maize for October-December delivery fetched 890 francs per tonne, against 900 francs paid on Tuesday.
"The maize decline is not over yet," one trader predicted.
Barley prices were unchanged as grain traders made no export bids through France at the European Union's last weekly export tender of the season.
"What for? This campaign is over," one dealer said.
Dealers said this suggested that the European Union's share of a large barley sale to Saudi Arabia would be covered by export licences already in the market and would thus be modest.
But a few traders said they still hoped the European Union would help facilitate the sale, either through a special export refund or through opening a new round of sales from intervention stocks.

Last week an EU official said the European Union was expected to provide 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of the 700,000 tonnes the Saudis bought and that this could mostly be covered by licences already in the hands of exporters.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
For 1996/97, the charges are as follows (francs per tonne).
